sources.title: Kosovo Visas
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Diaspora of the Republic of Kosovo
sources.officialityEvidence: The official Kosovo embassies platform publishes the inbound short-stay visa-exempt country list and its visitor-visa application procedure.
sources.supportingExcerpt: New Zealand is included in the list of countries whose citizens do not need a visa to enter Kosovo.

sources.title: Information for foreign citizens entering the Republic of Kosovo
sources.publisher: Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Kosovo
sources.officialityEvidence: Kosovo's Interior Ministry publishes the current admission and short-stay guidance for foreign citizens.
sources.supportingExcerpt: A foreigner may stay up to 90 days within a 180-day period, visa-free or with a visa when required.

policies.title: New Zealand ordinary passports: Kosovo visa-free short visit
policies.summary: Kosovo's official inbound visa guidance includes New Zealand among nationalities that do not need a short-stay visa.
conditions: Kosovo Interior Ministry guidance states a foreigner's short stay may be up to 90 days in each 180-day period, subject to ordinary admission conditions.
This does not classify work, residence, transit, special documents, means, address registration, health, security or final-admission requirements.

unresolved.reason: SafeTravel gives destination-risk advice and defers visa requirements to the destination authority. Afghanistan's reviewed official material provides generic visitor and visa categories but no current New Zealand ordinary-passport nationality schedule or issuance route. Generic visa wording is not normalized as advance issuance.

SafeTravel says independent tourism is not allowed. Current DPRK official material does not establish a New Zealand ordinary-passport visitor route, and practical border closure/restriction is not represented by the taxonomy.

The current SafeTravel page does not publish a passport-specific entry route for the Palestinian territories. Israel's ETA-IL material establishes travel authorization for Israel, not a standalone New Zealand-passport status for destination PS; checkpoint, permit, border-opening and Gaza conditions remain route dependent.

SafeTravel records unstable airport access; current Libyan government material does not establish a nationality-specific New Zealand ordinary-passport electronic, advance or arrival visitor route. The taxonomy has no airport-access or border-closure state.

No current BVI government source reviewed maps an ordinary New Zealand passport to a visitor visa exemption or issuance route. The broad named visa-required schedule is stale and is not used to infer a residual status.

Djibouti's official eVisa portal proves that electronic processing exists but publishes no reviewed nationality eligibility schedule for an ordinary New Zealand visitor passport. A portal form alone is not an eligibility finding.

Sudanese official material confirms visitor visas and counter processing but does not publish a New Zealand ordinary-passport exemption, advance-approval or arrival-issuance schedule. Generic visa wording is not normalized as advance issuance.

Iraq's federal eVisa portal presents a passport-country selector but its reviewed public country data do not establish New Zealand eligibility. Federal law's valid-entry-visa rule has named exceptions, so no residual eVisa or advance-visa route is inferred.

Current Syrian aviation material requires an entry visa unless exempt but does not publish the exemption cohort or a New Zealand ordinary-passport eVisa, advance or arrival route. It therefore cannot resolve the fallback electronic-visa label.
Comorian law describes visas subject to conventions and special laws but no current official nationality schedule establishes a New Zealand ordinary-passport advance, electronic or arrival route.

No reviewed current Cuban government source establishes a single New Zealand ordinary-passport tourist route; electronic and carrier/package routes are not a nationality-wide finding. The fallback eVisa label remains a hypothesis.

Turkmenistan's Migration Law establishes an entry-visa default subject to treaty exceptions, but current official material has no complete New Zealand ordinary-passport exemption, eVisa or airport-issuance schedule. A generic default does not establish pre-departure issuance.

No current official Ukrainian source reviewed directly establishes this ordinary New Zealand passport's visitor exemption and duration. SafeTravel destination guidance did not supply a route-specific classification; no fallback status is promoted.

No reviewed current Republic of the Congo source maps an ordinary New Zealand passport to a visitor route. The statutory foreigner rule preserves unspecified immigration agreements, and a historical eVisa project is not operational eligibility evidence.

Gabon’s current official air-entry eVisa notice and portal do not publish a New Zealand nationality eligibility matrix; the Foreign Ministry exemption register is stale. No residual electronic route is inferred.

South Sudan's MFA country table marks New Zealand as visa-required but does not state whether the visitor route is eVisa, advance mission issuance or arrival issuance. The Interior portal proves electronic processing, not this passport's route.

Tunisian official material establishes a general consular-visa rule and agreement-based waiver, but no current official New Zealand ordinary-passport schedule or effective agreement record was reviewed. No residual visa-free rule is inferred.

Current CEMAC material directly supports only its Member-State cohort. The Central African Republic embassy's online form is a mission process, not evidence of a New Zealand eVisa, arrival visa, or residual advance route.

The former Equatorial Guinea eVisa host currently serves unrelated content, and reviewed current CEMAC material supports only the Member-State cohort. No current New Zealand ordinary-passport route is established.

Reviewed current Panama Migration Service and Foreign Ministry material does not map a New Zealand ordinary passport to a visa exemption, stamped-visa, authorised-visa or normalized arrival/online route. Omission is not a visa-free inference.

No current Bosnia and Herzegovina official source reviewed directly establishes ordinary New Zealand passport visitor treatment. SafeTravel did not provide a route-specific entry classification, so the fallback visa-free label is not promoted.

Côte d'Ivoire's official SNEDAI process shows online pre-enrolment and biometric visa printing at Abidjan airport but no nationality eligibility schedule for a New Zealand ordinary passport. It cannot establish either an eVisa or, under this taxonomy, an arrival-issued visa.

Official ECOWAS material supports its separate member-national cohort, but no verified current Guinea-Bissau immigration or MFA schedule establishes New Zealand visitor eVisa, arrival, advance or exempt treatment.

Liberia's official visa-on-arrival process is mission/residence-dependent and requires online pre-approval; no direct New Zealand ordinary-passport baseline is published. The fallback eVisa label is not promoted.

No current reconcilable Malian nationality schedule or exhaustive residual rule establishes New Zealand visitor visa-free, electronic, arrival or advance treatment. The live MFA assistant is residence and filing-location dependent.
Niger's current MFA default preserves unenumerated bilateral and community exemptions. No current direct New Zealand nationality schedule establishes a visitor route; no residual status is inferred.

Nigeria Immigration Service confirms tourism eVisa or embassy routes outside ECOWAS and other waiver agreements, but does not publish a complete current ordinary-passport country-to-route or waiver-agreement list. New Zealand's route remains unproven.

No reviewed current Bangladesh government source establishes an ordinary New Zealand passport's visa-on-arrival eligibility or a nationwide electronic/advance route. The fallback arrival label is not promoted.

Chad's official eVisa page lists named exempt countries and says visa applications are online, but does not establish that every unlisted ordinary passport, including New Zealand, is required or eligible to obtain an eVisa. No residual route is inferred.

Cambodia's current official material names ASEAN and temporary PRC/HKSAR/Macao Tourist Visa T exemptions and says electronic Visa E is available for all countries. It does not establish New Zealand's current Tourist Visa T electronic or arrival route, so the fallback arrival label is not promoted.
